pr_title: iptables module: Enable support for pmtu clamp
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY

Fixes #82525

iptables has a native option to clamp the MSS within a rule to the path MTU. This patch enables support for this option. An example rule is:
```
iptables -A POSTROUTING -o eth1 -p tcp -m tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
```

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Feature Pull Request

issue_context.title: Add support for iptables TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
issue_context.body:
### Summary

I am attempting to use the iptables module in 2.13.0 to create an iptables rule for clamping MSS values on a specific GRE tunnel interface, however it appears that there is no option to set the `--clamp-mss-to-pmtu` flag anywhere for TCPMSS. To make this work I'm currently just using templates to replace the iptables-persistent files and load the rules from there, however this results in my docker rules being removed from the system as those are dynamically generated by docker which is not ideal to have removed.

### Issue Type

Feature Idea

### Component Name

iptables

### Additional Information

The equivalent iptables command would be the following:
```
iptables -A POSTROUTING -o tunnel200 -p tcp -m tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
```
I believe this should translate to the following task
```yaml
- name: Clamp MSS for GRE tunnels
  ansible.builtin.iptables:
    table: mangle
    chain: POSTROUTING
    out_interface: tunnel200
    protocol: tcp
    match: tcp
    tcp_flags:
      flags:
        - "SYN,RST"
        - "SYN"
      flags_set: []
    jump: TCPMSS
    clamp_mss_to_pmtu: yes
```

### Code of Conduct

```yaml

          flags_set:
            - SYN
```
